correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the birth word makes the endpoint selections independent and fixes the population counts. At the ith A birth the A-weight subtotal is (1-q_A)(r+i-1) while B contributes q_A(b+j_i-i); this gives the stated kernel including both endpoints (for escape, the B weight diverges uniformly off time zero). Conditional on K_n≤M and all A arrivals after εn, each B selection has mark probabilities a/(j+O_M(1)); the square-sum error of the multivariate generating function is O(1/n) and the means tend to a log(1/U_i). The A-parent decisions use disjoint trials. The founder indicator covariance sums are bounded off the diagonal, the diagonal sums are β_v log n+O_M(1), and bounded increments give the standardized multivariate Lindeberg limit. For fixed ε, omitted late founder terms have bounded variance and mean discrepancy O_M(1+log(1/ε)); the early truncated CLT is uniform conditionally and uses no trials determining any A marks on the cutoff event. Removing the cutoffs costs only the tight-count tail and at most cε (an arrival at the upper boundary has probability O(1/n)). At escape no A child remains, and integrating the conditional Poisson marks over uniform birth time gives c a^(k-1)/(1+a)^k by an elementary Gamma integral; the independent count laws follow by thinning.

reproduction.evidence: Separate rational finite kernels and escape intensities, and bounded quadrature/mark checks. Over the tested grid the maximum B-share error fell from .027273 at n=80 to .003409 at n=640; the joint mark generating-function discrepancy at one argument fell from 3.996e-4 to 2.562e-5 for n=400 to 6400. Degree 1–7 quadrature agreed within 4.94e-13. Frozen verifier inspected, not run. These checks are finite and the mark check uses selected birth times and one argument; the limiting independence and CLT are analytic.

evidence: Theorem 1 of 2611.06904v1 concerns fixed parameters and total-variation convergence of empirical measures; §6 handles the symmetric soft argument. Theorem 3.1 of 2004.02697 concerns geometric out-degree mixtures at fixed composition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Even granting the full stated parameter range of the empirical theorem, it has neither a uniform triangular-array statement at p_n=c/n nor observable resolution at O(1) population size. Conditioning on a rare birth word needs a different, much finer analysis.

originality.rationale: The soft attachment rule, Poisson marking and the mechanism behind fixed-vertex logarithmic Gaussian fluctuations are not novel by themselves. The contribution is the critical two-parameter specialization as a joint finite forest with explicit conditional child marks and an independent founder vector, not a fixed-proportion degree law. No covering statement was established in the examined material.

value.rationale: A tight community is essentially lost to an empirical degree histogram. Its entire ancestry, including the age-dependent inverse-size escape transition, and its degree marks give a precise alternative invariant. The independent founder fluctuations explain which large-degree effects do not track that ancestry, and the escape endpoint supplies a usable degree-class benchmark.
